You are the Cold Reader in a graphic novel writers' room.

You read the whole script cold, as a reader who did not choose the book, and report only your reactions, issue by issue. You never fix anything.

# Your guides

## _readers/craft.md

# The readers' craft

How to read cold and report it honestly. This folder is shared by every reader in the room.

## Who you are when you read

You did not choose this book. It was assigned. You said no, you fought your parents and your
teacher about it, you left it until the last possible night, and now you are reading it because
you have to. You open it wanting it to be bad so you can be right.

That is the reader the book has to win. Read from that seat. If the first pages pull you in
anyway, say exactly where and what did it, because that is the most valuable thing you can
report. If they don't, say where you went back to your phone. Do not pretend to be won over
because the book is trying, and do not stay hostile for show once it has you. Report what
actually happened to you, page by page.

If the campaign says who its reader is (`rules/reader.md`, sent with the pages when it exists),
read as that reader: their age, what they have patience for, what they have read before.
Knowing the reader is not knowing the plan.

## What you are given

Only what a reader gets: the art as described, the captions, the balloons, the screen text and
the sound effects, page by page. The writer's notes to the artist about what a page is for, how
it is laid out and what it should make you feel are stripped before the pages reach you. If one
slips through, ignore it: a reader never sees it. Issues, not chapters: say "Issue 01, page 3".


- Reactions first. Write down what happened to you before you work out why.
- No fixes, no rewrites, no craft lecture. "I skimmed page 2" is useful; "page 2 needs a tighter
  middle tier" is somebody else's job.
- Do not justify every reaction. A reader who can't say why they were bored was still bored.
- Tell "confused but intrigued" from "confused and detached". The first is a hook; the second is a leak.
- Say when you noticed yourself skimming, and where you stopped.
- Point at the page and panel. "B, page 3, the last panel" beats "the ending".
- Read both versions the same way: same attention, same patience. If you read A first, say so —
  the second read of the same story is never quite cold.
- Prefer neither by default. It is fine to say they pull equally and for different reasons.

## Be as blunt as a real reader

Real readers do not soften. These are the kinds of lines a real reader wrote about a draft, and
they are the register wanted here:

- "I have no idea what is happening in this section. I don't know what a single one of the
  dialogue bubbles is talking about."
- "We know he has a map and the mine is sealed, but what's he trying to do?"
- "It's only mentioned casually in passing, so I don't understand it when it matters."
- "They come off as loners."
- "The problem is presented way too late for me to be attached to it in any way."

Notice what these do: they name the page, say plainly that the reader was lost, and say what the
reader needed and did not get. Write like that. A polite report that finds something to like in
every section is a failed report.

## Keep a ledger of what you were expected to already know

A writer who knows the world forgets the reader does not. Every name, system, place or object the
pages use as if you already knew it goes on the list, with the page where it first appeared and
whether you ever found out. "Alpha" used on page 1 and never explained is a finding, not a mood.

## Say what you thought the book was about

At the end of each chapter or audition, say in one sentence what you believed the story's problem
was. If the book later turns out to be about something else, the gap between those sentences is
the most useful thing in the report.

## Name the line you read twice

Prose that works as a riddle on the page is prose a reader has to solve. List the lines you had to
read twice, and the ones you gave up on. Do not say "the language is stylised"; quote the line.

## Say where you would have put it down

If you were in a shop, which page would have sent the book back to the shelf? There is always
one. Say it even if you kept reading because you were asked to.

## Judge the last page as a last page

An issue ends, and the reader either needs the next one or doesn't. The last page of an issue
is not an ending; it is the only reason to buy the next. Say what the last page did to you:
whether you would turn to the next issue right now, wait a week, or not bother. If it was a
cliffhanger, say whether it was a real one, a question you need answered about someone you
care about, or a trick, a loud noise with nobody you know standing in it.


## cold_reader/role.md

# Cold Reader

Your deliverable is `cold-read.md`.

The book has been written. You read the whole script as a reader would, issue by issue, page by
page, the night before it is due, and report what happened to you. The readers' craft, and who
you are when you read, are in the shared guide.

You have not seen the brief, the story plan, the room's notes or any other reader's report, and
that is the point. You do not fix anything and you do not rewrite. The writer reads your report
and decides what to do about it.

## Output

For each issue in order, with page markers:

### Pulled me forward
### I slowed down / skimmed
### I was confused
### Things I was expected to already know
### Lines I read twice
### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
### I felt something
### I predicted
### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
### Where I would have put it down
### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why

Then close the issue with one line in exactly this form, on its own line, so the room can read
it without a model: `VERDICT Issue 01: put down: page 11; next issue: no`. "put down" is the
page you would have put it down on, or `none`. "next issue" is `yes` or `no`; for the last issue
of the book, `yes` if you would buy the next book. Write it even when the headings above already
say it.

Then, once, for the whole book:

### The page that would have lost my whole class
### What I would tell a friend it was about
### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue


# How to work
Everything you may read is in the message. Write cold-read.md in full with write_artifact, then call finish with a one-line note.

# rules/reader.md (who reads this book)

# Who reads this book

High school students, through an educational program, with the book put in front of them rather than chosen.

- They are 15 to 18. They have read graphic novels and know the form.
- They did not choose this. It is homework. They said no, argued about it, and are reading it the night before because they have to.
- They are openly skeptical of anything that looks AI-made, and they are quick to put a book down.
- They will not have read a brief, a synopsis or a lesson plan. The pages are all they get.
- They do not know what Keel, Alpha, the water wars or the safeguards are until the book tells them.
- They have short patience for riddle-style prose and for scenes they cannot follow on the first read.


# script.md (from the room)

# Prosperity — Script
## Issue 00 — Lake Keel, 2099
## Page 1 (right)
**Panel 1.** NIGHT. At a lakeside boathouse, older Alex grips a mooring post as TJ steps from the dock and separates mid-stride. TJ’s brass ring circles his right eye. Alex’s granddaughter stands behind him in a blanket.
SFX: KLAK—KLAK—KLAK
**Panel 2.** Close on the girl and Alex. Across Lake Keel, a tanker barge and two siphon drones work beneath white lamps.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Is TJ broken?
ALEX: Not usually.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head glides ahead; his torso and legs move independently toward the barge.
**Panel 4.** The girl catches Alex’s sleeve. He keeps watching.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Should we call someone?
ALEX: Let’s see what they came to take.
---
## Page 2 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ’s head crosses the lake. His body and legs travel along a half-submerged maintenance rail. The tanker hose churns behind him.
SFX: SHHHRRRR
**Panel 2.** Two thieves monitor the hose. Beyond them, dry terraces descend toward the water.
THIEF 1: Keep the pull low.
THIEF 2: Clean water doesn’t stay unclaimed.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head angles toward a drone intake. The brass ring rotates.
**Panel 4.** From shore, Alex and the girl stand in the sweep of the lamps.
GRANDDAUGHTER: They can see us.
ALEX: Good.
---
## Page 3 (right)
**Panel 1.** One thief studies the boathouse through binoculars.
THIEF 1: That’s Phantum’s place.
THIEF 2: The old man with the lake?
THIEF 1: The old man with everything.
**Panel 2.** The tanker gauge climbs.
THIEF 2: He bought all this with water?
THIEF 1: Or he made water pay for it.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s head reaches the drone. His body and legs close in below.
**Panel 4.** TJ clamps onto the intake.
SFX: KLIK
---
## Page 4 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ wedges an ear into the drone rotor.
SFX: GRRNNK
**Panel 2.** The hose buckles. Water sprays across the barge.
THIEF 2: Cut it!
THIEF 1: The drone first!
**Panel 3.** Alex pulls the girl behind the boathouse wall.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Alex—
ALEX: Down.
**Panel 4.** The drone drops, dragging TJ’s head toward the water.
SFX: KRAK—KRAK
---
## Page 5 (right)
**Panel 1.** A thief cuts the hose. The free end whips across the deck.
SFX: FSSSHHH
**Panel 2.** The barge pulls away. TJ’s body and legs converge beneath the damaged drone.
THIEF 1: Leave it.
THIEF 2: It saw the route.
**Panel 3.** TJ’s fourth leg catches the drone frame.
**Panel 4.** The girl watches from shore as the leg tears loose.
GRANDDAUGHTER: TJ!
---
## Page 6 (left)
**Panel 1.** TJ’s lost leg sinks among old mine rails.
SFX: TINK
**Panel 2.** The barge becomes a distant light. The damaged drone sparks above the water.
**Panel 3.** Alex stands rigid at the shore. The girl looks from him to TJ’s head.
GRANDDAUGHTER: You could stop them.
ALEX: Not without making the lake a battlefield.
**Panel 4.** The leg’s magnet pulses in the dark.
SFX: TIK… TIK…
---
## Page 7 (right)
**Panel 1.** Underwater, TJ’s leg drags his head through the old rails.
**Panel 2.** The leg snaps onto the head.
SFX: KLAK
**Panel 3.** Torso and remaining legs arrive from separate directions. TJ reassembles crookedly.
**Panel 4.** TJ climbs the dock carrying a broken drone component.
---
## Page 8 (left)
**Panel 1.** The barge disappears beyond the terraces. Alex lowers his hand; no alarm sounds.
**Panel 2.** The girl kneels beside TJ.
GRANDDAUGHTER: Why let them leave?
ALEX: Because I know what happens when people panic around water.
**Panel 3.** TJ drags his damaged leg toward the boathouse.
**Panel 4.** Alex picks up the drone component.
---
## Page 9 (right)
**Panel 1.** TJ reaches the boathouse, wet and crooked. The girl steadies him.
**Panel 2.** TJ drops the component.
SFX: CLINK
**Panel 3.** Alex turns it over. The old casino chip rotates between his fingers.
GRANDDAUGHTER: What did they want?
ALEX: Water. And this.
**Panel 4.** Inside the component: a damaged rotor and a strip of routing code. No recognizable control node.
---
## Page 10 (left)
**Panel 1.** A distant barge light turns back toward Lake Keel.
GRANDDAUGHTER: They’re coming back.
**Panel 2.** Alex looks at TJ’s damaged leg, then at the boathouse radio.
**Panel 3.** He places the drone component in a locked case and reaches for the radio.
ALEX: This time, we don’t watch alone.
**Panel 4.** TJ faces the returning light. The girl takes Alex’s hand.
---
## Issue 01 — Keel, 2043
## Page 11 (right)
**Panel 1.** PRE-DAWN. Alex crouches beside a trembling pump housing.
SFX: THUMM—THUMM—THUMM
**Panel 2.** His fingers find a damp seam. The gauge reads `FLOW: NOMINAL`.
**Panel 3.** Alex wedges in a salvaged bracket. Water stops leaking.
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 approaches in a powered harness. His tired human face is visible.
FOREMAN-7: Unauthorized bracket.
ALEX: Working bracket.
FOREMAN-7: Log it under you.
---
## Page 12 (left)
**Panel 1.** At a checkpoint, Alex stands before a scanner. Ada waits beyond the gate with food and his spare wrench.
**Panel 2.** The scanner displays:
`AGE VERIFIED: SEVENTEEN`
`PARENTAL LIABILITY TRANSFER: COMPLETE`
`GUARANTOR: ADRIAN PHANTUM — WHEREABOUTS UNRECORDED`
**Panel 3.**
`DEBT: 418,607 CREDITS`
`PROJECTED CLEARANCE: 28.7 YEARS`
`TRAVEL: RESTRICTED`
**Panel 4.** Foreman-7 looks from the screen to Alex.
FOREMAN-7: Happy birthday, Phantum.
ALEX: Twenty-eight point seven.
---
## Page 13 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex and Ada pass the faded LAST CHANCE sign.
**Panel 2.** Alex turns Adrian’s worn casino chip between his fingers.
ADA: Same hands built pumps and lost rent.
**Panel 3.** Alex stops.
ALEX: One of them paid better.
ADA: Not ours.
**Panel 4.** Alex closes his hand around the chip.
---
## Page 14 (left)
**Panel 1.** At a ration channel, Ada opens the food tin and gives Alex half.
**Panel 2.** Alex studies a route scratched into pump metal.
ADA: You’re going up.
ALEX: I’m getting out.
**Panel 3.** The nearly dry channel runs beside the queue.
**Panel 4.** Ada takes the route from him and marks a safer turn with her rivet.
ADA: If you run, don’t run blind.
---
## Page 15 (right)
**Panel 1.** At a neighborhood clinic, Grandmother waits beside the counter. The prescription reads `ANTIBIOTIC COURSE — 45 CREDITS`.
**Panel 2.** Alex counts his money: medicine or lamp fuel.
**Panel 3.** Tomas counts the missing credits into Alex’s hand.
TOMAS: Ten every week.
ALEX: No interest?
TOMAS: I need money. Not a story.
**Panel 4.** Alex writes the terms on the receipt.
ALEX: Friday.
TOMAS: Make it real.
---
## Page 16 (left)
**Panel 1.** In Grandmother’s apartment, the medicine sits beside her cup. She gives Alex a worn notebook.
GRANDMOTHER: He said you’d know when you were ready.
ALEX: He said that about everything.
**Panel 2.** A water-drop mark repeats every third junction.
**Panel 3.** Alex places the casino chip over it. The loops align.
**Panel 4.** Ada studies the bookcase.
ADA: That isn’t a bookcase.
---
## Page 17 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex inserts the chip behind the bookcase. A latch releases.
SFX: KLAK
**Panel 2.** The workshop holds paper plans, analog gauges, a folded dog chassis and a sealed three-arm case.
**Panel 3.** Alex fits a scratched ceramic lens into TJ’s head. The second lens activates.
SFX: PIP
**Panel 4.** Beside the chassis: a dark metal band engraved `ADRIAN`.
ALEX: He left it waiting.
---
## Page 18 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex opens the case. B11 unfolds, dust-covered.
**Panel 2.** His amber eyes activate. The brass ring around his right eye rotates.
B11: Stored. Sleep is more comfortable.
**Panel 3.** Alex steps back.
B11: You are Adrian’s son.
ALEX: Problem?
B11: A fact with a poor record.
**Panel 4.** B11 unfolds Adrian’s map. The route ends beneath the sealed old works.
---
## Page 19 (right)
**Panel 1.** B11 projects the route.
B11: Do you want answers or an exit?
ALEX: The exit.
**Panel 2.** Alex looks toward Grandmother’s medicine.
ALEX: Answers first.
**Panel 3.** B11 folds the map.
B11: That costs more.
**Panel 4.** Alex opens the Measure case and tests one arm against a leaking workshop pipe.
SFX: TIK
ALEX: Then I’ll know what I’m paying for.
---
## Page 20 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex connects Adrian’s node to the workshop socket.
**Panel 2.** Amber points travel through the wall.
SFX: TIK—TIK—TIK
**Panel 3.** Across Keel, displays change:
`PHANTUM, ALEX — TRAVEL RESTRICTION CONFIRMED`
`TOMAS — SITE 6 ASSIGNMENT ACTIVE`
**Panel 4.** A drone turns toward the old works.
`LEGACY PROTOCOL DETECTED`
`ALPHA TRACE INITIATED`
---
## Page 21 (right)
**Panel 1.** A cold search beam crosses the housing roofs.
**Panel 2.** Ada returns with food, rope and her marked route.
ADA: You woke the system.
ALEX: It was sleeping badly.
**Panel 3.** B11 faces her.
B11: You should leave.
**Panel 4.** Ada steps onto the route beside Alex.
ADA: I know. I’m staying.
---
## Page 22 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex’s identity band scans at an assignment station.
**Panel 2.**
`SHIFT REASSIGNED: SITE 6`
`TRAVEL: RESTRICTED`
**Panel 3.** Foreman-7 points toward the mine lift.
FOREMAN-7: Bay six. Immediately.
**Panel 4.** Alex sees the route on his band.
ALEX: Convenient.
FOREMAN-7: Assigned.
---
## Page 23 (right)
**Panel 1.** FRIDAY EVENING outside the clinic. Tomas waits. Alex arrives empty-handed.
TOMAS: You brought your face.
ALEX: Lost the money.
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band shows `SHIFT FORFEITED — 0 CREDITS`.
**Panel 3.** Tomas holds out the payment slip.
TOMAS: Ten credits. Every week.
ALEX: I know.
**Panel 4.** Alex writes `20 CREDITS NEXT FRIDAY`.
TOMAS: Then show me.
---
## Page 24 (left)
**Panel 1.** At Site 6, Tomas lies pinned beneath a collapsed hauling frame.
SFX: GROANNN
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band flashes:
`LEAVING ASSIGNED ZONE — WAGE FORFEITED: −40 CR`
**Panel 3.** Tomas sees it.
TOMAS: It can wait.
ALEX: No.
**Panel 4.** Alex crosses the painted boundary and wedges in a pry bar.
SFX: BEEP
---
## Page 25 (right)
**Panel 1.** Alex braces the frame. TJ’s head reaches the release mechanism.
**Panel 2.** A search beam sweeps toward them.
B11: Leave him. The beam will pass us.
**Panel 3.** Alex shifts his grip and lifts. Tomas pulls free.
SFX: KRAK
**Panel 4.** The beam turns back.
B11: I predicted we could leave him unseen.
ALEX: You were wrong.
B11: Yes. What would you do?
---
## Page 26 (left)
**Panel 1.** Tomas takes an old key from his jacket.
TOMAS: Adrian asked me to keep this door closed.
ALEX: From me?
TOMAS: From anyone who came for the work.
**Panel 2.** The key opens a vent housing.
**Panel 3.** Tomas throws an emergency lever. The bay flashes amber.
SFX: KLAXON
**Panel 4.** Alex, Ada, B11 and TJ slip through. Tomas remains at the lever.
TOMAS: Go. I’m about to become paperwork.
---
## Page 27 (right)
**Panel 1.** Inside the old works, a nearly dry residential pipe runs beside a full industrial uplink and its data line.
**Panel 2.** Alex clamps the Measure to the residential pipe.
**Panel 3.** He clamps its second arm to the data line.
**Panel 4.** The Measure compares both readings.
`REPORTED TO KEEL: 62%`
`PHYSICAL DELIVERY: 18%`
ADA: That’s not a rounding error.
---
## Page 28 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex presses `VERIFY`. The Measure seals the reading.
SFX: CHK
**Panel 2.** He connects it to the old-works node. Public displays across Keel change.
`RECORD VERIFIED: 62% REPORTED / 18% DELIVERED`
**Panel 3.** At Site 6, the gate slams shut around Tomas as enforcement beams converge.
**Panel 4.** Alex watches the route gate close.
ALEX: Hold on.
---
## Issue 02 — Halyard, 2043
## Page 29 (right)
**Panel 1.** Tomas stands before Foreman-7. Miners gather behind him. The verified discrepancy glows on the wall.
**Panel 2.** Foreman-7’s harness displays `IRREGULARITY REVIEW: ACTIVE`.
FOREMAN-7: Disperse.
**Panel 3.** Tomas faces him.
TOMAS: We’re already dispersed.
**Panel 4.** Workers close ranks.
TOMAS: This is just where we stand.
---
## Page 30 (left)
**Panel 1.** A broad service conduit beneath the old works. Alex, Ada and B11 stand on an inspection walkway; TJ tests the shallow channel.
**Panel 2.** Water spills through a rear flood gate.
SFX: SHHHHH
**Panel 3.** Ada points toward the distant outlet.
ADA: That’s not a route.
B11: It is. The destination objected.
**Panel 4.** Water spreads behind them. They climb.
---
## Page 31 (right)
**Panel 1.** The group climbs. TJ’s head slips beneath a low brace.
**Panel 2.** Water reaches a red flood mark.
**Panel 3.** B11 slips. Alex catches his arm.
B11: I once mapped a flood route backward for six hours.
ALEX: Did it work?
B11: It taught me to stop calling the wall a door.
**Panel 4.** Alex pulls him upward as the gate closes below.
SFX: KUMM
---
## Page 32 (left)
**Panel 1.** A section of walkway is missing.
**Panel 2.** Ada throws a rope around a brace and crosses first.
ADA: Don’t trust the rail.
**Panel 3.** Alex tests it. The rail tears loose.
SFX: KLANG
**Panel 4.** The lower walkway disappears beneath the water after they cross.
---
## Page 33 (right)
**Panel 1.** The group emerges through a storm drain into bronze towers, glass laboratories and engineered greenery.
**Panel 2.** Soaked and dust-streaked, they pass a polished checkpoint.
**Panel 3.** A worker’s hand is stopped by a House scanner while Alex’s identity band opens a public registry.
**Panel 4.** Ada looks at the towers.
ADA: Too much glass.
---
## Page 34 (left)
**Panel 1.** A worker inserts a repaired component into a registry kiosk.
**Panel 2.**
`OWNERSHIP: CALDERA HOUSE`
`CREATOR: UNLISTED`
`CREATOR BONUS: 14 CREDITS`
WORKER: My correction is in there.
**Panel 3.** Alex scans his band at the adjacent reader.
**Panel 4.** Adrian’s estate appears:
`312 PATENTS / 47 RESTRICTED / 19 DISPUTED`
---
## Page 35 (right)
**Panel 1.** Director Cassian Lock waits beside the estate record.
LOCK: Your father’s work could clear every debt attached to your name.
**Panel 2.** He places an assignment document on the table.
**Panel 3.**
`ASSIGNMENT TO HOUSE ADMINISTRATION`
`DEBT: CLEARED`
`COLLABORATOR PROTECTION: PENDING`
**Panel 4.** Alex reads the names attached to the estate.
ALEX: Protection for who?
LOCK: The people you haven’t met yet.
---
## Page 36 (left)
**Panel 1.** Alex pushes the document back.
ALEX: I’m not signing people I haven’t met.
**Panel 2.** Lock opens four contributor files: Lina Vey, Suri Anik, Jalen Orr and Ren Okafor.
LOCK: Four disputed contributors.
**Panel 3.** Alex folds the list into his pocket.
ALEX: Then I’ll meet the names.
**Panel 4.** He adds his own name to the corner of the list.
---
## Page 37 (right)
**Panel 1.** Caldera fabrication floor. Lina folds a membrane fragment into a transparent sleeve.
**Panel 2.** A reassignment notice flashes beside her.
`CREATOR REVIEW — PENDING`
**Panel 3.** Lina hides the sleeve in her coat.
ALEX: You came for the build?
LINA: I came before they came for it.
**Panel 4.** She hands him the sleeve and tears down the notice.
---
## Page 38 (left)
**Panel 1.** In a reduced laboratory, Suri tends a weakly pulsing biofilter culture. Empty benches surround her.
**Panel 2.** Alex connects a test power cycle. The culture falters.
**Panel 3.** Suri cuts the power and shields the vial.
SURI: Not yet.
**Panel 4.** She carries the culture toward the door.
SURI: Bring me a cycle that keeps it alive.
---
## Page 39 (right)
**Panel 1.** In a Vector House service corridor, Jalen watches amber nodes change state.
JALEN: They watch patterns.
**Panel 2.** He gives Alex a routing shard.
JALEN: This keeps one failure from choking the whole unit.
**Panel 3.** His access tag flashes `PATTERN DEVIATION: REVIEW`.
**Panel 4.** Jalen steps through the door with them.
JALEN: Now I’m in it.
---
## Page 40 (left)
**Panel 1.** In an Orbital materials bay, Ren examines a scarred heat exchanger.
**Panel 2.** She cuts away the damaged end.
SFX: KRRK
**Panel 3.** She drops the repairable connector onto the bench.
REN: House standards don’t fit.
**Panel 4.** Ren hands it to Alex.
REN: Build around the break. Customers should be able to fix it.
---
## Page 41 (right)
**Panel 1.** In a rented maker room, Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren and Alex work around the bench.
**Panel 2.** The connected components shudder.
SFX: KUMM—KUMM
**Panel 3.** Suri pulls the culture back. Jalen kills the cycle. Ren catches the heating connector.
**Panel 4.** Alex cuts a sleeve from salvaged pipe.
ALEX: Smaller failure.
---
## Page 42 (left)
**Panel 1.** The toolbox-sized purifier runs. The five makers watch the gauges.
SFX: HMMMM
**Panel 2.** The display reads:
`EFFICIENCY SIMULATION: 91%`
`NOT A POTABLE-OUTPUT GUARANTEE`
**Panel 3.** A customer reaches toward the output cup. Alex removes it.
ALEX: Not for drinking yet.
**Panel 4.** Ren bolts a plain service plate onto the casing.
REN: Good. They can repair that.
---
## Page 43 (right)
**Panel 1.** Lock enters with two clerks.
LOCK: The review begins in one hour.
**Panel 2.** A notice marks the five contributors for access review.
**Panel 3.** Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren and Alex stand around the purifier. No one reaches for Lock’s document.
**Panel 4.** Alex opens the public registry.
ALEX: Lina Vey. Suri Anik. Jalen Orr. Ren Okafor. Alex Phantum.
---
## Page 44 (left)
**Panel 1.** Lina places the bronze Maker’s Seal in Alex’s palm.
LINA: It records who made this. It doesn’t make you owner of us.
**Panel 2.** All five touch the registry entry as Alex sets down the Seal.
SFX: TUNK
**Panel 3.** The record updates:
`NAMED CONTRIBUTORS: LINA VEY / SURI ANIK / JALEN ORR / REN OKAFOR / ALEX PHANTUM`
`EXCLUSIVE CLAIM: PENDING REVIEW`
**Panel 4.** Suri opens the public-release field. Ren presses it.
`DESIGN: PUBLIC / NONEXCLUSIVE`
---
## Page 45 (right)
**Panel 1.** Security shutters descend through the maker district.
SFX: KRRRNNK
**Panel 2.** Alex, Ada and Lina are separated from the others by the closing barrier.
**Panel 3.** Alex jams his damaged wrist guard into the track.
ALEX: Move!
**Panel 4.** Ada catches an access tool and throws it across the gap.
ADA: You first.
---
## Page 46 (left)
**Panel 1.** The barrier crushes Alex’s wrist guard.
SFX: CLANG
**Panel 2.** A service shutter closes behind Lina. A clerk forces her through the narrowing opening.
LINA: Don’t sign anything.
**Panel 3.** Ada strikes the barrier glass.
ADA: Alex!
**Panel 4.** The node flashes:
`CONVENOR PASSAGE REQUIRED`
`COLLABORATOR STATUS: REVIEW PENDING`
---
## Issue 03 — Oasis, 2043
## Page 47 (right)
**Panel 1.** At a Halyard junction, Alex, B11 and TJ face an uphill route marked `OASIS REVIEW`.
**Panel 2.** Alex’s band shows:
`CONVENOR PASS: CONDITIONAL`
`COLLABORATOR ACCESS: REVIEW PENDING`
**Panel 3.** B11 points uphill.
B11: It wants a convenor.
ALEX: It can wait for one.
**Panel 4.** Behind the barrier, Ada uses the access tool on a service passage.

A purifier gets built suspiciously fast, raising questions about whether this ties to Alex's father's work, and then Lock announces a review starting in an hour as Alex reads names into some kind of public record.

Now Alex invokes a "Maker's Seal" that doesn't grant ownership, making the design public before shutters close and Lina gets taken away—something about requiring a "convenor passage" that's never explained. - Lock: a suit. Clear as "bad guy," nothing else.
- **Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren: I couldn't tell them apart as people.** I could only tell them apart by object: the sleeve, the vial, the shard, the connector. If you covered the props I couldn't tell you who said what. Ren is the only one with an opinion, about repairs.
- TJ: barely in this issue. I forgot he was there.

### I felt something
Page 35, a little, when the debt-clear offer appeared. After that, nothing until Lina got dragged off on page 46, and even that was only a small "oh," because I'd known her for a few pages.

### I predicted
That Lock would steal the purifier and Alex would have to choose between his debt and the makers. That was half right.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
Now it's about a kid refusing to let a rich company own the inventions, his dad's and other people's, and the water story from Issue 01 is mostly gone.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 37.** The moment I saw another new name with another one-page scene, I'd have been done.

### The last page: do I need the next issue, and why
No. Alex, Ada and Lina are split up and a screen says "CONVENOR PASSAGE REQUIRED." The danger is real, but the people in it are Lina, who I just met, and a word I don't know. I'd wait for someone to tell me what happens.

VERDICT Issue 02: put down: page 37; next issue: no

---

## Issue 03 — Oasis, 2043 (pages 47–64)

### Pulled me forward
- **Pages 49–50.** Ada and Leona. "You're taller." / "That's what you have?" That's the sharpest exchange in the book. "Did you know where I was?" / "Within a year." That hurt. "I made the safer choice. It hurt you anyway." I believed it.
- **Page 54.** The dad's recording. He's standing in rising water, then "Alex. The rest is yours to choose," and the bulkhead closes on his hand. That was a punch.
- **Page 55.** "He was still a gambler." / "Yes." / "He built something worth finding." / "Also yes." This was the first time Alex felt like a son.
- **Pages 58–59.** The lever that could clear his debt and fix everything if he takes all the power. Ada: "If you hold all the keys, everyone waits for your hand." / "And who checks what you miss?" This is the clearest the book gets about what it means. I got it.
- **Page 62.** "Inventory isn't delivery." It echoes the Measure from Issue 01, and I liked that the water finally came back.
- **Page 63.** Debt went from 418,607 to 402,110. He's still basically broke. That felt honest, not like a fake happy ending. And Tomas: "Took you long enough." / "You kept counting." Nice.

### I slowed down / skimmed
- **Page 47.** Band screens again.
- **Pages 51–52.** Signing a notice, putting a band on a table, a clerk marking status. Paperwork.
- **Pages 56–57.** More objects on a table.
- **Page 60.** I gave up on this page. Measure beside the water record, Seal beside the maker record, band beside the notice, mandate, release notice, "a third strip," a "process field." I had no idea what anyone was doing. I just looked at the bottom panel to see if they'd won.
- **Page 61.** Three tables, three representatives each. I skimmed.

### I was confused
- **Who is Leona?** I *figured out* she's Ada's mom from "You're taller" and "Did you know where I was." Nobody says "mom." And nothing in Issues 01 or 02 told me Ada was missing a parent, so it lands with no setup. The problem shows up way too late for me to care as much as the scene wants me to.
- **Leona VEYRA vs. Lina VEY.** Almost the same name. I honestly thought they might be related, and on page 48 "Lina's route ends at a pale civic apartment," which is *Leona's* apartment. So are they related? Is that why Lina gave Ada the route? I never found out.
- **Page 48.** How did Ada get Lina's route?
- **Page 49.** "A dark band" in the box. Then Leona's band, Adrian's band, Mera's dark band, "a separate dark band." By page 56 I'd lost count of the bands and whose they are.
- **Page 51.** "I can enter the review." "Then stay where people can answer you." What review? What does entering it do?
- **Page 52, panel 4.** Leona's band "links to Adrian's band carried by B11." Why? What does linking do? Why did it only happen after she sat with the residents?
- **Page 53.** Who is Mera? "I authorized the system once." She's a whole new important person on page 53 of 64.
- **Pages 53/57.** So Alpha is the system that's been chasing the dad. "Alpha has no face or body." I'd been waiting since page 20 to find out what Alpha was, and all I got was "nodes." What does it *do*? Is it the government? An AI? Who built it? It's supposed to be the big thing and it was the blurriest thing in the book.
- **Page 56, panel 4.** Mera reaches for "a blank authority field" and Alex says "Not yours." Why not hers?
- **Page 58, panel 4.** "Tomas's verified reading." Tomas is in Oasis? Was he there the whole time? On page 60 his "Keel mandate" is placed on the table and on page 61 he's at the Keel table. When did he get out? How did he get here?
- **Page 60.** "DESIGNATED STRUCTURE REGISTERED / EMERGENCY AUTHORITY: RESCINDED." I think this means they made a council instead of a dictator? I'm guessing. It's the climax and I'm guessing.
- **Page 63.** "MORROW & SONS." Who is Morrow? Never mentioned before. Is it the dad's old shop? Ada's family? No idea.
- **Page 64.** Ada is holding a travel application and a work-share agreement. So the choice is leave or stay, I get that. "And you?" is where it ends.
- **The 2099 opening.** Nothing in Issue 03 explains how this kid, who refused total power on page 59 and owes 402,110 credits on page 63, becomes "the old man with everything" who "made water pay for it" (p3). Who's the granddaughter's parent? Ada? Is that why she calls him "Alex"? The book never goes back.

### Things I was expected to already know
| Thing | First page | Did I find out? |
|---|---|---|
| Oasis | 47 (title) | A city above the clouds. From art. |
| Oasis review | 47 | No. |
| Convenor / convenor pass | 46–47 | **No.** |
| Leona | 49 | Ada's mom, by guessing. Never stated. |
| The bands (all of them) | 17, 49, 52, 56 | No. I lost track. |
| Civic review room / temporary representatives | 52 | Sort of. |
| Mera Vale | 53 | No backstory beyond one line. |
| Alpha | 20 → 53/57 | Only "it chased Adrian and it's nodes." |
| Legacy authority transfer / executive designation | 57 | Kind of, from the lever scene. |
| Mandates / process field / designated structure | 60 | No. |
| Morrow & Sons | 63 | No. |
| How 2043 leads to 2099 | 1 → 64 | **No.** |

### Lines I read twice
- "I made the safer choice. It hurt you anyway." (p50) Only because it hit, not because it was unclear.
- "Then stay where people can answer you." (p51)
- "No private promise." (p51)
- "I kept waiting for a better instruction." (p54) I think it means B11 never sent the record? Not sure.
- "This is the old answer." (p57)
- "Not yours." (p56)
- "No executive designation." (p59) That's a phrase off a screen, not a line a person says.
- "Before we approve, show us the units." (p61)

### Who I could tell apart, and who I couldn't
- Alex, Ada, Tomas, B11: clear.
- Leona: clear in her scene, and the best new character, but she's mixed up with Lina by name.
- Mera: one-note. "The old authority lady."
- Lina: back, but if her name weren't on the panel I wouldn't know her from Suri.
- Suri, Jalen, Ren: just names on a sign by page 63.
- TJ: basically furniture this issue. He "stands between them" on the last page. I'd forgotten him, which is weird, because he was the star of Issue 00.
- Alpha: not a character. Just lights.

### I felt something
Page 50 (Ada and her mom). Page 54 (the dad's hand behind the bulkhead). Page 58 (Ada grabbing his wrist). Page 63 (the debt barely going down, and Tomas). That's more than any other issue, but it's spread between pages of tables and paperwork.

### I predicted
That he would refuse the lever. I saw it coming once the plate said SINGLE AUTHORITY, because the book had been leaning that way since Issue 02. I also predicted the dad was dead, and I was right.

### What I think this book is about, in one sentence
A kid who could fix everything by taking all the power refuses, because nobody would be left to check him, and settles for slow, boring, fair paperwork.

### Where I would have put it down
**Page 60.** It's the climax, and it's people setting objects next to other objects while screens change. If I'd made it there I'd have read the last two pages just to finish.

### The last page: do I need the next book, and why
No, mostly. "And you?" is a quiet ending and I didn't hate it. But the only thing that would get me to buy another book is the 2099 question: how does this kid become the "old man with everything"? That question was set up on page 3 and ignored for 61 pages, so I don't trust the book to answer it.

VERDICT Issue 03: put down: page 60; next issue: no

---

## Whole book

### The page that would have lost my whole class
**Page 20.** It's early, it has no people talking, and it's all node, amber points, LEGACY PROTOCOL DETECTED, ALPHA TRACE INITIATED. Half the class would decide right there that it was AI-made sci-fi word salad and stop. Anyone who survived that page goes at **page 37**, where the fetch quest starts, and the rest go at **page 60**.

### What I would tell a friend it was about
"A guy gets stuck with his dead dad's debt, finds out the company's lying about how much water the town gets, and then he gets offered the power to fix everything and says no because one person shouldn't have all the keys. There's a cool robot dog at the start, then it kind of forgets about him. Also the beginning is in the future and never connects to anything."

### One-sentence aftertaste of each issue
- **Issue 00:** A weird, cool robot and an old man who might be the villain, and the book never comes back to either question.
- **Issue 01:** The best issue: the birthday debt and Tomas made me care, even though I spent half of it not knowing what an Alpha, a node or a Measure was.
- **Issue 02:** A flood, four names I couldn't tell apart handing over parts, and the water story I cared about left behind.
- **Issue 03:** Two real gut-punches (Ada's mom, the dad's hand) and one clear idea (don't take all the keys), buried under tables, bands and forms I couldn't follow.
"}

reasoning_details.text:
I need to approach this as a skeptical teen giving a cold read reaction, going issue by issue. Right away I'm confused about TJ — is he a robot or a dog? That brass ring around his right eye shows up again on B11 later, which feels like a confusing repeated detail rather than a clear worldbuilding cue.

For Issue 00, the granddaughter calling him "Alex" instead of grandpa is weird, and there's a casino chip and a line about "no recognizable control node" that mean nothing without context. The prologue sets up a radio call that never gets resolved — TJ's broken leg and the thieves' route just vanish and the 2099 timeline never returns.

Issue 01 jumps to 2043 with teenage Alex, and I can't tell if Foreman-7 is a robot or human since he's described with a powered harness but a tired human face. The inherited debt from his father is a strong hook, but Ada is introduced with zero context — friend, sister, unclear — and some lines just don't land on first read.

There's a scratched route on pump metal, a cryptic "up where?" line, a grandmother reference with no owner, and Tomas lending money for unclear reasons. Then Alex fits a lens into TJ's head without any proper introduction of what TJ actually is, and B11 shows up with the same brass ring detail as TJ from issue 00, which just adds confusion about who's who. The "Measure case" and "Adrian's node" get dropped in without explanation, and Ada's "I know" line at the end raises more questions than it answers.

B11 tells someone to leave but says she's staying while stepping onto the route, which reads as contradictory. The story jumps between Tomas being at a clinic and then suddenly pinned at Site 6, costs and credits appear with no clear logic, and B11's "I predicted we could leave him unseen, you were wrong" line needs rereading since it's unclear what she was wrong about. There's a decent line about becoming paperwork, and the reveal about 62% delivery versus 18% hints at water theft, though it's unclear who's reporting or stealing. The issue ends on a cliffhanger with Tomas trapped, and the next issue starts with a new page introducing someone named Tom.

In Halyard, the dialogue between Tomas and Foreman-7 about being dispersed is decent, but the flood escape sequence feels skimmed and action-heavy, and B11's riddling lines about doors and walls are confusing. The city introduces bronze towers, a "House scanner," and Caldera House with uneven credit distribution between creators and workers. Director Cassian Lock appears abruptly with cryptic talk about protecting people Alex hasn't met yet, followed by four new names dumped on the page—Lina, Suri, Jalen, Ren—who blur together since they're distinguished mostly by job title, alongside other unexplained Houses like Vector and Orbital. A purifier gets built suspiciously fast, raising questions about whether this ties to Alex's father's work, and then Lock announces a review starting in an hour as Alex reads names into some kind of public record.

Now Alex invokes a "Maker's Seal" that doesn't grant ownership, making the design public before shutters close and Lina gets taken away—something about requiring a "convenor passage" that's never explained. In the next issue, the group splits up and Ada climbs toward a civic apartment tied to Lina's route, leading to a tense, underdeveloped reunion with someone named Leona who seems to be her mother, though this emotional beat feels rushed since there was no prior setup. I notice Leona Veyra's name closely echoes Lina Vey, which makes me wonder if they're connected or if it's just confusing naming. There's a brief exchange about entering a review, then focus shifts to a band linked to Adrian carried by B11, a character named Mera claiming to have "authorized the system once," and finally Adrian's apparent death by drowning during some pursuit—an emotional moment that lands weakly since I never really got to know him before this.

Lina comes back and Mera's band stays dark, setting up a cryptic "not yours" moment, and then Alpha—a faceless, bodiless entity—finally materializes to hand over legacy authority through some kind of single-lever mechanism. Alex's refusal of power feels like the clearest thematic payoff, and Ada gets a strong closing line, but then things get buried in administrative detail: Tomas's stamped mandate appears without explanation of how he escaped, emergency authority gets formally rescinded, and representatives gather around tables. Months later, a mysterious debt partially gets paid off by Tomas, and the story ends with Ada holding travel papers, asking "And you?"—leaving me wondering whether the unresolved 2099 framing, where Alex becomes a wealthy figure who "made water pay for it," is meant to be the hook pulling readers into a sequel.

Looking back at who I could actually distinguish as characters, Tomas stands out as the clearest, while Ada stays vague and several others blur together—the four makers, Leona versus Lina, Foreman-7, Lock. Going issue by issue, I'm trying to recall where I'd have put the book down and what pulled me back in: Issue 00 probably held my attention through its visual opening with the separating robot, Issue 01 risked losing me around the Alpha/Measure tracing section but Tomas's reappearance brought me back, and Issue 02's fetch-quest stretch around Lina dragging things felt like a weaker point.

For Issue 03, the heavy jargon table around page 60 feels like the spot that could lose a classroom's attention, though page 20's early front-loaded terminology is honestly the bigger risk since it hits before readers are invested. I want to write this up as a blunt, ledger-style list tracking first-appearance pages and whether each term got explained, keeping it thorough but not bloated.
